item.title: UnionPay connects the world through seamless digital payments
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
UnionPay connects the world through seamless digital payments UnionPay International and Armenian Card reach agreement on online acceptance cooperation, Sept. 3, 2026. (Photo courtesy of UnionPay International) When Indonesian tourist Nur arrived at Shanghai Pudong International Airport alongside her daughter, she began what had long been a dream vacation: exploring China's cultural and natural landmarks. "We plan to take a high-speed train to Huangshan Mountain in Anhui province, then visit Jingdezhen and Sanqing Mountain in Jiangxi province. We want to explore as much as possible and experience the beauty of China firsthand," Nur said excitedly. "On this trip, I plan to pay for everything with GoPay, something that would have seemed impossible just a few years ago." GoPay, one of Indonesia's leading digital wallets, now works seamlessly with China's payment ecosystem following the launch of cross-border QR code interoperability between the two nations earlier this year. "Chinese users can scan QR codes to pay at merchants in Indonesia using apps such as UnionPay, while Indonesian users can simply scan and pay with digital wallets such as GoPay at UnionPay- and Alipay-accepting merchants in China," an executive of Chinese payment giant UnionPay said. Over the years, UnionPay has evolved from a domestic card network into a global payment infrastructure provider, linking bilateral and multilateral payment systems to support seamless merchant acceptance, card issuance, and mobile payments worldwide. Today, UnionPay's digital payment capabilities extend across multiple continents. Travelers can scan QR codes for retail and dining purchases in Thailand, Malaysia, and some other Southeast Asian markets. In the Middle East, including the United Arab Emirates, visitors can settle bills at airports and in commercial hubs without needing to exchange cash. Across Africa, particularly in South Africa, UnionPay cards are widely accepted for hotel bookings, transportation, and daily expenses. Globally, UnionPay is now accepted in 183 countries and regions, spanning more than 100 million merchants outside the Chinese mainland and connecting around 2,600 member institutions. UnionPay cards have been issued in 86 countries and regions outside the Chinese mainland, and the company has partnered with overseas institutions to launch more than 200 digital wallets based on UnionPay standards. Furthermore, through QR code interoperability agreements with countries including Indonesia, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Argentina, and Türkiye, UnionPay has enabled over 46 million overseas merchants to accept mobile payments from its global base. UnionPay International and National Payment Corporation of Kazakhstan reach agreement on QR code interoperability, June 18, 2026. (Photo courtesy of UnionPay International) UnionPay is also playing an active role in the transformation of the global payments industry. In recent years, through a "single-point connection" model, it has established interoperability with QR code payment networks in multiple countries and regions. It has also provided countries such as Laos and Thailand with payment switching and clearing systems and technical standards, and participated in developing domestic QR code payment standards in Singapore and Thailand. These efforts mark a shift from simply expanding its network to helping shape the rules of the industry. "Take South Asia for example. The local payments industry is still at an early stage of development, and many institutions have limited technical capabilities. External service providers charge high fees and require lengthy development cycles," a UnionPay executive said. "Our cloud-based card issuance platform, which keeps system upgrade costs low, has enabled us to bring three local institutions on board to issue UnionPay cards. Tailoring solutions to the specific circumstances and pain points of local institutions is a key principle behind successful cooperation," the executive added. By sharing its technology and standards, UnionPay has helped reduce payment costs in some Belt and Road partner countries, enabling them to share in the benefits of digital payments. UnionPay's services not only help Chinese consumers and businesses go global but have also become part of everyday life in many countries and regions. UnionPay cards are used by local residents in the United Arab Emirates, Kenya, Mongolia, Singapore, Kazakhstan and Bangladesh as salary cards and student cards, among other purposes. In Bangladesh, for example, UnionPay has issued millions of cards through long-standing partnerships with local financial institutions, making it one of the international card networks with the largest cardholder bases in the country. At a supermarket in the Indonesia Morowali Industrial Park (IMIP), a checkout terminal displays the acceptance interface of Indonesia's national unified QR payment system QRIS. Shoppers can scan QR codes to pay via Chinese payment platforms Alipay and UnionPay. (Photo by Fan Jiageng) UnionPay has become one of the most widely recognized Chinese service brands overseas. Nielsen, a market research and data analytics company, forecasts that UnionPay will rank first globally in the number of cards in circulation by 2030. With its ever-expanding global network, UnionPay is making cross-border payments increasingly convenient. "Keeping pace with China's continued expansion of high-standard opening up, UnionPay connects the world through payment services, building financial links between China and other countries that facilitate the flow of funds and foster closer ties between peoples," a UnionPay executive said. item.title: Beijing forum calls for open, collaborative, inclusive ecosystem for financial development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
Beijing forum calls for open, collaborative, inclusive ecosystem for financial development BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- High-profile guests gathered in Beijing on Monday for the opening of the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2026. With a theme of "Building an Open, Collaborative and Inclusive Ecosystem for Global Financial Development," this year's conference is attracting prominent guests from home and abroad who will participate in various activities, including the main forum, parallel forums, thematic conferences and side events during the four-day event. During the opening ceremony, Yin Li, secretary of the Communist Party of China Beijing Municipal Committee, said that Beijing has become an important bridge connecting Chinese and foreign financial markets. He said the capital city is ready to deepen financial exchanges and practical cooperation with all parties, jointly build an open and interconnected financial market ecosystem, and create a world-class business environment that is market-oriented, law-based, convenient and internationalized. The forum, inaugurated in 2012 as a platform for global exchange and cooperation in the field of finance, has grown into a major source of updates on China's financial policies, providing a window into the work priorities of the financial sector in the world's second-largest economy. Pan Gongsheng, governor of the People's Bank of China, China's central bank, said the central bank has actively promoted the transformation and improvement of China's monetary policy framework, further enriched its monetary policy toolkit, and made the market-based interest rate regulation mechanism clearer. Going forward, the central bank will assess and improve the monetary policy framework, continue to raise the level of RMB internationalization, further strengthen high-quality policy supply, and explore the application of artificial intelligence in areas such as assisting with monetary policy situation analysis and financial risk identification. Pan also unveiled that the central bank will join with other financial authorities to introduce a number of policy measures. These include establishing a liquidity support facility to address large-scale redemptions by non-bank institutions, expanding the range of institutions eligible for the Standing Lending Facility, and promoting connectivity between the interbank and exchange bond markets. Other policy measures to be introduced include pilot measures to facilitate foreign financial institutions' RMB purchase and sale business in the onshore foreign exchange market, and issuing guidelines regarding financial support for building international science and technology innovation centers in Beijing (Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region), Shanghai (the Yangtze River Delta), and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, according to Pan. Ding Xiangqun, head of the National Financial Regulatory Administration (NFRA), said that the NFRA is enhancing the effectiveness of regulation, adopting a risk-based approach to strengthen financial supervision, improving the financial rule of law in line with practical needs, and strengthening regulatory capacity in key areas. Ding said the NFRA remains committed to actively expanding new space for financial opening-up, supporting international economic and trade exchanges, and improving the global financial governance system. Regarding the capital market, Wu Qing, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), said the CSRC will make every effort to safeguard its safety and stability by closely tracking market dynamics at home and abroad, strengthening risk assessment and the policy toolkit, and enhancing risk prevention for new types of businesses. According to him, China will facilitate cross-border investment and financing by enhancing the convenience of investment operations through the Qualified Foreign Institutional Investors scheme. Foreign-funded entities are encouraged to leverage their parent companies' professional expertise and strengths to further refine their product portfolios and participate in innovative business areas in China, Wu added. Fu Hua, president of Xinhua News Agency, said at the opening ceremony that creating a favorable public opinion climate for financial reform and development is an important part of building a new ecosystem for financial development, adding that Xinhua stands ready to make an effort toward that end. Zhu Hexin, head of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), said a batch of incremental measures will be rolled out to better support enterprises in engaging in international cooperation and competition. These include facilitation measures for the current account to better meet the diverse settlement needs of foreign trade enterprises and support the development of new forms and models of trade, and measures to optimize foreign exchange management under the capital account to better meet enterprises' needs for cross-border investment, financing and fund allocation, and expand two-way investment cooperation. Zhu revealed that China intends to expand its pilot program that allows securities companies to conduct foreign exchange settlement and sales business, and support financial institutions in providing exchange rate risk management services to enterprises. The annual conference, which runs from Oct. 19 to 22, is jointly hosted by the Beijing Municipal People's Government, the People's Bank of China, the NFRA, the CSRC, Xinhua News Agency and the SAFE. item.title: China's top economic planner vows more efforts to expand domestic demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
China's top economic planner vows more efforts to expand domestic demand BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China's top economic planner said Tuesday it will work with relevant departments to expand domestic demand with greater force and more effective measures. More efforts will be made to vigorously boost consumption, Zuo Gang, an official with the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), said at a news conference. Authorities will raise the share of public service spending in fiscal expenditure, strengthen inclusive policies that reach consumers directly, and promote the expansion and upgrading of goods consumption, including new energy vehicles and smart products, Zuo said. The push comes as consumption shows signs of steady improvement. Total retail sales of goods and services rose 2.6 percent year-on-year in the first three quarters of 2026, with retail sales of services growing faster than goods and new forms of consumption continuing to emerge, official data showed. Final consumption expenditure contributed more to overall economic growth in the January-September period. Zuo said China will invest in both physical assets and human capital to expand effective investment. Specifically, the NDRC will push for the implementation of the 109 major projects outlined in the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) and the "six networks" initiative, covering water, power, computing, communications, urban underground pipelines and logistics networks, Zuo said. Ultra-long special treasury bond funds will be deployed more effectively, and the new policy-based financial instruments will be used at a faster pace, Zuo said, also vowing stronger support for social welfare, technology innovation, industrial upgrading and security resilience. China's investment is undergoing a profound shift in emphasis from traditional sectors to emerging ones, analysts said, noting that artificial intelligence and new infrastructure will serve as key engines for the next round of effective investment. Official data showed the country's investment in innovation-driven sectors held up well in the first three quarters of 2026, even as overall fixed-asset investment continued to contract. Investment in intellectual property products rose 9.3 percent year-on-year in the January-September period, while investment in high-tech industries grew 4.9 percent. Investment will increasingly serve the development of new quality productive forces and the building of a modern industrial system, with the ultimate results felt in expanded employment, rising incomes and improved living standards, said Liu Yuanchun, president of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics. item.title: China's Q3 economy picks up pace, reinforcing role as global growth engine
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
China's Q3 economy picks up pace, reinforcing role as global growth engine An aerial drone photo taken on Sept. 18, 2026 shows a view of Tianjin Port in Tianjin, north China. (Xinhua/Sun Fanyue) BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's economy picked up pace in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, supported by fast-growing new drivers and fresh policy support, staying on track to meet its annual growth target and remaining a leading engine of global growth. China's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 4.5 percent year on year in Q3, higher than the second quarter's reading of 4.3 percent, data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed Monday. The world's second-largest economy generated about 107.11 trillion yuan (about 15.94 trillion U.S. dollars) in output during the January-September period, expanding 4.6 percent year on year, according to the NBS. "The national economy forged ahead against pressure and continued to shift toward innovation-driven, high-quality development, with growing positive changes in major indicators," the NBS said in a statement. China has consistently contributed around 30 percent of global economic growth, with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva saying in January that this contribution is expected to stay at roughly the same level in the coming years. Tourists visit the Anshun ancient town in Anshun City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Oct. 6, 2026. (Photo by Lu Wei/Xinhua) GROWING RESILIENCE Noting that the GDP growth of 4.6 percent in the first three quarters is in line with the country's annual growth target, NBS deputy head Mao Shengyong told a media conference that the economy added 5.7 trillion yuan in output during the period, the largest increase for the same period in the past five years. In the third quarter, GDP growth picked up 0.2 percentage points from the second quarter, while some international institutions expected major economies to grow more slowly in July-September compared to the April-June period, Mao said. There was also a notable rise in momentum on a monthly basis. In September, value-added industrial output rose 5.5 percent year on year, 0.3 percentage points faster than in August, while the services production index gained 4.8 percent, up 0.7 percentage points from the previous month. Retail sales of consumer goods grew 1.1 percent in September, 0.7 percentage points faster than in August, and the surveyed urban unemployment rate edged down 0.1 percentage points from August to 5.2 percent. "Growth momentum showed signs of marginal improvement in September," said Wen Bin, chief economist with China Minsheng Bank, citing faster industrial and services output, a rebound in consumption and an initial stabilization of investment. China will step up efforts to expand domestic demand, improve supply, and make macro policies more effective to sustain the positive momentum of innovation-led and high-quality development, Mao said. To this end, China has recently rolled out a batch of new policies, including financial and fiscal support. "With existing policies being implemented faster and incremental policies gradually taking effect, the economy is expected to continue improving in the fourth quarter," Wen said. Humanoid robots are seen under training at an intelligent manufacturing plant for commercial vehicles of the Dongfeng Liuzhou Motor in Liuzhou City, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Jan. 30, 2026. (Photo by Zheng Changhao/Xinhua) NEW DRIVERS AT WORK New growth drivers continued to expand, contributing more than 40 percent to China's economic growth in the first three quarters. Value-added industrial output rose 5.3 percent year on year, with equipment manufacturing up 10.2 percent and high-tech manufacturing up 14.3 percent. Output of industrial robots, lithium-ion batteries and 3D printing equipment jumped 29.1 percent, 39.5 percent and 62.5 percent, respectively. Monday's data also showed that the services sector expanded 5.2 percent year on year in the first three quarters, with information transmission, software and IT services up 10.4 percent, and leasing and business services up 12.3 percent. The shift is visible in the economic structure. Manufacturing accounted for 25.7 percent of GDP in the first three quarters, up 0.6 percentage points from a year earlier, while the share of high-tech manufacturing in the value-added output of major industrial enterprises rose 1.6 percentage points. Investment in intellectual property products climbed 9.3 percent. Traditional industries are also moving up the value chain. In Jingdezhen, a ceramics hub in east China's Jiangxi Province, local producers have embraced 3D printing in pottery making, propelling the sector's output to over 100 billion yuan. Meanwhile, some coal mining companies have implemented smart monitoring systems for underground operations, increasing efficiency by 30 percent. Green development is creating openings as well. The penetration rate of new energy vehicles in China has stayed above 60 percent for six consecutive months, while the country's energy consumption per unit of GDP fell 3.1 percent in the first three quarters. "The foundations of the economy remain solid, while new quality productive forces, modern services and high-tech foreign trade are steadily taking root," said Zhu Qigui, associate director of the China Academy of Financial Research. "As long as China continues to rely on innovation, reform and its vast market, the trend of moving toward new and better development will not change," the scholar said. A drone photo shows new energy vehicles to be exported at Yantai Port in east China's Shandong Province, Sept. 15, 2026. (Photo by Tang Ke/Xinhua) SHARED OPPORTUNITIES A major trading partner of as many as 169 countries and regions, China saw its goods trade rise 18.8 percent year on year to 39.94 trillion yuan in the first three quarters. In September alone, trade grew 27.5 percent. In the first nine months, exports of mechanical and electrical products climbed 23.7 percent and accounted for 64.3 percent of total exports, while intermediate goods made up more than half of all exports, reinforcing China's role as a stabilizing anchor for global industrial and supply chains. In east China's Anhui Province, robotics manufacturer EFORT Intelligent Robot Co., Ltd. has continued to see growth in overseas orders this year, with a batch of its spraying robots set to be exported to Italy. The company's overseas revenue increased by more than 50 percent year on year in the first half of 2026. Meanwhile, the company's client, German automobile giant Volkswagen, is shifting its strategy from "in China, for China" to "in China, beyond China," with cars produced in China already exported to the Middle East and Central Asia. Foreign-invested enterprises in China remained active players in the January-September period, with their imports and exports rising 19 percent to 11.69 trillion yuan, a record high for the same period. Their trade in intermediate goods grew 27.4 percent to 7.9 trillion yuan, and their high-tech product exports jumped 42.1 percent. More foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0," deepening their integration into China's industrial and innovation chains, Mao said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China to advance new legislation on cultural heritage protection
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
China to advance new legislation on cultural heritage protection BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China will work to advance the formulation of a cultural heritage protection law as part of efforts to better preserve and pass on its cultural heritage, an official said Tuesday. Hu Kaihong, deputy director of the General Office of the Central Commission for Guiding Cultural and Ethical Progress, told a media conference that the move is outlined in the country's first five-year plan dedicated to cultural heritage protection issued in September. The plan calls for improving the legal and regulatory framework and strengthening legal safeguards for various types of cultural heritage, including historic and cultural districts, said Hu, also director of the office of the central commission for cultural heritage protection. Hu said the plan for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) prioritizes protection, promotes the rational use of cultural heritage and adheres to the principle of minimal intervention, while strengthening systematic protection and unified oversight. The plan sets a target of fully identifying the country's cultural heritage resources by 2030, with an improved regulatory framework, a stronger body of laws and regulations, and a growing pool of professionals. China is home to 61 UNESCO World Heritage sites, including the Great Wall, the Mogao Caves and the Beijing Central Axis. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Overseas buyer attendance at first phase of China's Canton Fair hits record high
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
Overseas buyer attendance at first phase of China's Canton Fair hits record high This photo taken on Oct. 18, 2026 shows a scene at the venue of the 140th Canton Fair in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province. The on-site exhibition of the first phase of the 140th edition of the China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, concluded here on Monday. As of October 19, the fair has attracted 189,000 overseas buyers from 214 countries and regions, a 13.3 percent increase from the session of the same period last year and a new high, according to the China Foreign Trade Centre (CFTC), the organizer of the fair. (Xinhua/Deng Hua) GUANGZHOU, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- The first phase of the 140th China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, concluded its in-person exhibition on Monday, with overseas buyer attendance reaching a record high. As of Monday, 189,000 overseas buyers from 214 countries and regions had attended, up 13.3 percent from the same period of the previous session, said the China Foreign Trade Center, the fair's organizer. It added that the record turnout highlights the resilience and vitality of China's foreign trade. The first phase, themed "Advanced Manufacturing," covered 520,000 square meters, with more than 25,000 booths and over 12,000 participating enterprises. The exhibition showcased the latest products and technologies across five sectors and 19 exhibition areas, including electronics and home appliances, industrial automation, lighting and electrical equipment, hardware and tools, and new energy vehicles and smart mobility. The fair is divided into three phases, all taking place in Guangzhou, the capital of south China's Guangdong Province, and running through Nov. 4. The second phase, themed "Quality Home Life," will run from Oct. 23 to 27 and feature building materials and furniture, household items, gifts and decorations, among other categories. Serving as a barometer and wind vane of China's foreign trade, this year's fair, marking its 70th anniversary, highlights innovation, intelligence, greater specialization and higher quality. Over the past 70 years, the Canton Fair has grown into China's largest and longest-running international trade event, with the most complete product range, the largest number of buyers and the highest transaction volume. Guangdong, a manufacturing hub and trade powerhouse, on Monday reported that its quarterly foreign trade exceeded 3 trillion yuan (about 446 billion U.S. dollars) for the first time in the third quarter of 2026. The data came as China's foreign trade maintained solid momentum in the first three quarters of 2026. The country's total imports and exports rose 18.8 percent year on year to 39.94 trillion yuan in the January-September period, official statistics showed. item.title: Commentary: Resilient Chinese economy brings much-needed certainty to the world
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
Commentary: Resilient Chinese economy brings much-needed certainty to the world A drone photo shows new energy vehicles to be exported at Yantai Port in east China's Shandong Province, Sept. 15, 2026. (Photo by Tang Ke/Xinhua) BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- Viewed as an ocean rather than a pond, China's economy may not be immune to headwinds, but it stands firm enough to absorb powerful waves and weather turbulent times. In a world starved of certainty, it remains a stabilizing force in the global economy. Facts on the ground speak for themselves. China's economy expanded by 4.6 percent in the first three quarters of 2026, landing squarely within the full-year target range and remaining among the fastest of major economies. Yet to read the economy solely through the lens of headline speed is to miss the more important story. China is in a critical period of accelerating the transition from old growth drivers to new ones. The quality of growth and the direction of structural change matter more. New quality productive forces are gathering momentum, with new growth drivers including high-end manufacturing, the digital and intelligent economy and modern services contributing more than 40 percent of expansion. In particular, industrial robots, 3D-printing equipment and lithium-ion batteries all registered strong double-digit growth, helping steer the economy toward more innovation-led, quality-driven development. The foundation of China's economic resilience also lies in consumption, which accounted for nearly half of the GDP growth in the first three quarters. Services retail sales, upgraded goods consumption, new formats, as well as lower-tier markets and inbound tourism, are all picking up steam. With policymakers leaning harder into consumption support, household spending appetite is showing steady signs of recovery, setting the stage to unlock the vast potential of the country's super-large market. Foreign trade remains one of the brightest spots, with growth reaching its highest level for the same period in five years. From new energy vehicles to photovoltaic products, robotics and innovative pharmaceuticals, Chinese exports are increasingly defined by frontier technology, original innovation capability and complete industrial and supply chains. Furthermore, China has ample and effective policy tools to shape its economic growth trajectory. Five-year plans, deepened reforms and wider opening up, along with targeted fiscal and monetary measures and considerable room for counter-cyclical adjustment, all provide predictability and stability for the market. A clear-eyed understanding of the Chinese economy also requires acknowledging the real headwinds: a complex and volatile external environment, insufficient domestic demand, and a structural transition that isn't finished. As the latest figures have demonstrated, the Chinese economy is resilient. This is contrary to the narratives hyped up by certain pessimists and doomsters in the West. Backed by a domestic market of 1.4 billion people, a solid manufacturing base, well-developed infrastructure, a strong talent pool, and complete industrial and supply chains, the underlying fundamentals and long-term positive trend remain unchanged. Amid the sluggish global recovery and rising geopolitical risks, China's development continues to offer the world growth momentum and market opportunities. It is both a sustained driver of inclusive and shared growth and a reliable buffer against global economic volatility stemming from factors such as regional conflicts and the rise of unilateralism and protectionism. For many years, China has contributed around 30 percent of global economic growth, remaining a major engine of the world economy. As the world's largest manufacturer, China continues to provide high-quality, affordable, and reliable product supply globally. No longer just the world's factory, China is becoming a market and a mega-buyer for the world as imports have surged over 20 percent, reflecting a more balanced and open trade structure. China's commitment to opening up remains unwavering despite rising protectionism globally. This is evidenced by the establishment of more new foreign-invested enterprises, and also highlighted by Apple's executive chairman Tim Cook, who recently noted that the company remains optimistic about China's development prospects and will further expand its business in the country. China's edge may lie less in its speed, but more in the quality and sustainability of its advance, and in its capacity to hit its full-year targets. "China Opportunity 2.0," boosted by the dividends of innovation and high-standard opening up, will surely create more win-win cooperation outcomes for the world. item.title: BeiDou Navigation Satellite System drives economic growth and social development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
BeiDou Navigation Satellite System drives economic growth and social development An operator uses a BeiDou-guided agricultural drone to apply precision crop protection treatments over a paddy field in Pingpu township, Wuhu, east China's Anhui province. (Photo/Xiao Benxiang) From satellite constellations in space to ground-based terminals, and from transport and emergency response to smart cities, agricultural production, and maritime navigation, China's BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) has steadily expanded its global footprint in recent years. By strengthening industrial support capabilities and deepening its international reach, the system is providing new momentum for economic and social progress worldwide. In July 2026, BDS completed a comprehensive in-orbit upgrade of its entire satellite constellation. "The upgraded system now provides nationwide real-time positioning at centimeter-level accuracy, alongside globally covered high-precision positioning featuring rapid convergence, "said Gou Ping, chairman of China Satellite Network Group Co., Ltd. "It also supports up to one billion connected terminals, including 100 million consumer devices and one million industrial units, all operating with sustained reliability." The delivery of high-precision, highly stable, and highly reliable positioning, navigation, and timing services across all environments forms the foundation for the large-scale application of the BDS. Zhang Nu, chairman of China Time and Space Information Group Co., Ltd., said that more than 70 mobile phone models worldwide now support the BDS short-message communication function, with more than 450 million users having activated the service. Looking ahead to the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), China will coordinate the deployment of space-based and ground-based navigation augmentation resources, and promote the integration of the BDS with low-Earth-orbit navigation augmentation systems, 5G and 6G, inertial navigation, LiDAR, vision-based technologies, and other sources of positioning and timing information. The goal is to build a multi-level, three-dimensional integrated positioning and navigation system, extending seamless positioning and timing services from outdoors to indoors and from the deep sea to deep space. In Waigang township, Jiading district, Shanghai, a new model of intelligent farming is taking shape across more than 667 hectares of high-standard farmland. With support from BeiDou technology, various types of smart agricultural machinery are carrying out the entire rice production process, from plowing and planting to crop management and harvesting. "Automatic navigation and driving systems for agricultural machinery equipped with next-generation BDS positioning terminals offer greater accuracy and more stable signals. They are already being used on farms in western and northern China," said Liu Bolin, head of planning at Shanghai-based company ComNav Tech. Farm operators drive BeiDou-enabled harvesters to harvest early rice in Taihe county, Ji'an, east China's Jiangxi province. (Photo/Deng Heping) During the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025), the BDS-related industry grew by more than 53 percent. By late 2025, BDS applications had extended across key sectors, including transportation, energy, urban development, emergency response and disaster mitigation. The system is continuing to expand into new fields and application scenarios, such as the low-altitude economy, the marine economy, and cultural, sports and tourism events. Consumer adoption is accelerating rapidly. "On Feb. 22 this year, Amap recorded one trillion BDS positioning requests in a single day, supporting a total daily navigation distance of 9 billion kilometers," said Liu Zhenfei, chairman of Amap, a leading provider of digital maps in China. China is improving policies to support and guide the industry, strengthening collaboration among industry, universities, research institutions and end users, and promoting coordinated development among upstream and downstream players and businesses of all sizes across the BeiDou industrial chain. Under the leadership of China Time and Space Information Group Co., Ltd. and other organizations, a new technical framework for short-message communication using space-time information has been released. It has helped reduce the cost of short-message chips by 70 percent and driven shipments of chips using the new framework to 50 million units. As one of four global navigation satellite systems officially recognized by the United Nations, BeiDou-related hardware and software solutions have now reached more than 140 countries and regions worldwide. "Space technology has increasingly become an important component of digital infrastructure and the digital economy," said Chea Vandeth, Cambodia's minister of post and telecommunications and chairman of the Digital Government Committee. Together with other global navigation systems, the BDS has enhanced the diversity, availability and resilience of global satellite-based positioning, navigation and timing services, the minister added. Expanding the international application of the BDS on a larger scale and promoting international cooperation in satellite navigation serve the shared interests and aspirations of countries around the world. BeiDou-enabled autonomous guided vehicles transport containers at a fully automated container terminal of Rizhao Port in east China's Shandong province. (Photo/Tang Ke) Deep in the deserts of Saudi Arabia, Sinopec Geophysical Corporation, a subsidiary of China Petrochemical Corporation, is leveraging high-efficiency 3D seismic acquisition technology to help local oil firms explore for oil and gas resources. "Every geophone point across thousands of square kilometers and each shot point for vibrator trucks demand high-precision positioning and time synchronization," explained Wang Zhongwen, a production operations expert at the Sinopec BeiDou operation and service center. By integrating the BDS with spatio-temporal information terminals, the project has greatly boosted construction precision and operational efficiency, cutting the re-survey rate by 85 percent. According to a 2026 report on the development of the BDS industry, compiled by the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, BeiDou's global outreach is shifting from a product-export model toward a comprehensive ecosystem approach that seamlessly integrates hardware, software solutions, managed services, and partner networks. item.title: Xi congratulates Central Institute of Socialism on 70th founding anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
Xi congratulates Central Institute of Socialism on 70th founding anniversary BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday sent a congratulatory letter to the Central Institute of Socialism, celebrating its 70th founding anniversary. In the letter, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, praised the institute for training a large number of non-CPC representatives who share the CPC's ideals and work in unity toward common goals, and for making important contributions to consolidating and developing the patriotic united front over the past 70 years. He encouraged the institute to continue strengthening political training, building broad political consensus, and improving the quality of its teaching and research as well as its governance capacity. Xi called on the institute to play a greater role in training talent for the united front, conducting theoretical research and promoting principles and policies, so as to better serve the overall work of the CPC and the country.
